BlitzLLVM is a compiler and runtime for BlitzBasic, Blitz3D and BlitzPlus programs. It builds your code into a native executable with LLVM and draws it with Vulkan and SDL3, so projects that were written for the original tools can run on current systems. It is free and open source.

Drop-In replacement for Blitz3D and BlitzPlus

Programs written for Blitz3D or BlitzPlus will just work without any changes necessary. While BlitzLLVM offers additional features, its priority is entirely on being nearly 100% compatible with the originals. Pick up your ancient projects and release an updated version that works on modern systems.

Easy to Write, Easy to Learn!

BlitzLLVM keeps the Basic syntax you know, and it is as quick to pick up as ever. Every download comes with tutorials and sample games, so you can start from working code instead of a blank file. Whether this is your first program or your hundredth, there is plenty to build on, and the tutorials cover the newer features as well as the classic ones.

Native Performance

Programs are compiled and optimized by LLVM, the same compiler infrastructure behind many modern native applications. The compiler and runtime are designed to run fast on even the oldest x86-64 (64bit) hardware, as long as a GPU is available. And with some extra work, even x86 (32bit) is possible.

Proper Warnings and Errors instead of Crashes

BlitzLLVM reports mistakes that the original compiler let through silently, such as code that is legal but probably not what was meant. It also ships additional tools, like blitz-tidy which fixes simple mistakes in your source files, and blitz-format which formats a whole project to a configurable single style.

Multi-Platform and Multi-Arch

Compiled programs run natively on Windows, Linux, and macOS under x86-64 and arm64. No compatibility layers or emulation required - unless you use platform specific user libraries. Additional targets are available via LLVM cross-compiling options with some additional requirements.

Proper Input Handling

Raw input gives direct access to mice, keyboards, joysticks, wheels and gamepads, and any number of them can be used simultaneously. Thanks to proper hot plug detection, devices which disconnect and reconnect are reassigned to their appropriate port and keep working.

Modern Image, Model, Sound and Video Formats

Textures, models, sound and video load from the classic formats as well as newer ones such as WebP, JPEG XL, AVIF, glTF, Ogg Opus, MP4 and MKV.

Free and Open Source

BlitzLLVM only uses free and open source libraries, and the source code is open. The licenses of everything it includes are shipped with every download.
